summary: Frontiers plays like a leaner Star Realms built for one or two people at a table with fewer external inputs needed, using scorecards to drive solo objectives or a shared threat in co-op mode. Turns are the same fast trade-for-ships-then-attack loop, but the ship pool is smaller and more curated than base Star Realms plus Colony Wars.
praised: Fast, satisfying deckbuilding loop that's easy to teach
Works well solo or two-player without needing a full group
Combines cleanly with other Star Realms sets for more variety
criticised: Feels thin as a standalone purchase if you already own base Star Realms
Solo/co-op scorecard objectives can feel gamey or repetitive over many plays
Less tactical depth than the head-to-head competitive mode
Card pool overlap with other Star Realms products can feel redundant

interaction.kind: open conflict and take-that combat, or shared cooperative threat

scoring.why: Whoever reduces the opponent's Authority to zero first wins, or in solo/co-op mode the scorecard objective is met before the shared threat overwhelms the players
